name: Monstera Deliciosa
short_description: The one everyone starts with, and still the best value for the space it fills.
description:
Fast, forgiving and happy in most rooms as long as it is out of direct sun. The splits in the leaves come with age and light: a young plant with plain leaves is not a different plant, it is a younger one.

  • Light: Bright, indirect
  • Water: When the top 5 cm is dry, about weekly
  • Pets: Mildly toxic if chewed
  • Grows to: 2 m indoors
  • Difficulty: Easy

reviews.author: Priya N.
reviews.content: Arrived better packed than anything I have ordered. Already put out a new leaf, split and all.

reviews.author: Cal R.
reviews.content: Bigger than I expected for the 17 cm, which is a good problem. One leaf was creased in transit.

name: Fiddle Leaf Fig
short_description: Architectural, dramatic, and famously opinionated about being moved.
description:
It wants one bright spot and to be left in it. Turn it a quarter each week so it grows evenly, water when the top third of the pot is dry, and accept that it will drop a leaf after any change of scene.

  • Light: Bright, some direct sun
  • Water: When the top third is dry
  • Pets: Toxic if chewed
  • Grows to: 2.5 m indoors
  • Difficulty: Fussy

name: Snake Plant
short_description: The plant for a dark hallway and a bad memory for watering.
description:
It will survive a month of neglect and a north-facing wall. The only reliable way to kill one is to keep it wet, so water it when the soil is dry all the way through and then leave it alone.

  • Light: Low to bright
  • Water: Every three to four weeks
  • Pets: Mildly toxic if chewed
  • Grows to: 80 cm
  • Difficulty: Very easy

reviews.author: Dee M.
reviews.content: In the darkest corner of a north-facing flat for four months and it has not blinked.

name: Pothos Marble Queen
short_description: Trails a metre in a season and tells you plainly when it is thirsty.
description:
Marbled cream and green, happiest trailing from a shelf. The leaves go soft when it needs water and recover within the hour, which makes it the best plant to learn on.

  • Light: Low to bright, indirect
  • Water: Weekly, when the leaves soften
  • Pets: Mildly toxic if chewed
  • Trails to: 1.5 m
  • Difficulty: Very easy

name: ZZ Plant
short_description: Glossy, upright, and nearly impossible to kill by forgetting it.
description:
It stores water in rhizomes under the soil, which is why it copes with a dark office and a fortnight away. Wipe the leaves twice a year and they stay polished.

  • Light: Low to medium
  • Water: Every three weeks
  • Pets: Toxic if chewed
  • Grows to: 90 cm
  • Difficulty: Very easy

name: Peace Lily
short_description: Flowers in a room most plants only survive in, and faints theatrically when dry.
description:
White spathes two or three times a year in medium light. It wilts dramatically when it wants water and stands back up within a couple of hours, which is alarming the first time and useful after that.

  • Light: Medium, indirect
  • Water: When it starts to droop, about weekly
  • Pets: Toxic if chewed
  • Grows to: 60 cm
  • Difficulty: Easy

name: Rubber Plant
short_description: Deep green, almost black in low light, and grows a foot a year.
description:
Broad leathery leaves on a single stem that you can prune to branch. Bright indirect light keeps the colour dark; direct sun scorches it, and a cold draught makes it drop the lowest leaves.

  • Light: Bright, indirect
  • Water: When the top 5 cm is dry
  • Pets: Mildly toxic if chewed
  • Grows to: 2 m indoors
  • Difficulty: Easy

name: Calathea Orbifolia
short_description: Silver-striped, pet safe, and honest about hating hard water.
description:
Beautiful and particular: it wants humidity, filtered or stood water, and no direct sun. Crisp brown edges mean the air is too dry. Worth it for the leaves, which fold up at night.

  • Light: Medium, indirect
  • Water: Keep just moist, filtered water
  • Pets: Safe
  • Grows to: 70 cm
  • Difficulty: Fussy

name: Spider Plant
short_description: Pet safe, nearly indestructible, and gives you free plants all summer.
description:
Arching striped leaves and runners that make babies you can pot on. Copes with most light, most watering habits and most rooms, which is why it has been in every kitchen since 1974.

  • Light: Bright to medium, indirect
  • Water: Weekly in summer, less in winter
  • Pets: Safe
  • Grows to: 50 cm, plus runners
  • Difficulty: Very easy

name: Parlour Palm
short_description: Pet safe, happy in shade, and Victorian in the best sense.
description:
It grew in unheated drawing rooms for a century and still asks for very little: shade, an occasional drink, and no direct sun. Slow, so what you buy is roughly what you keep.

  • Light: Low to medium
  • Water: When the top 5 cm is dry
  • Pets: Safe
  • Grows to: 1.2 m, slowly
  • Difficulty: Easy

name: Aloe Vera
short_description: Wants a sunny sill and to be forgotten between waterings.
description:
A succulent, so the usual rules invert: full sun, gritty compost, and a soak only once the soil is bone dry. Overwatering is the one thing it will not forgive.

  • Light: Direct sun
  • Water: Every three to four weeks, soak and drain
  • Pets: Mildly toxic if chewed
  • Grows to: 50 cm
  • Difficulty: Very easy

name: String of Hearts
short_description: Pet safe, trails a metre, and looks like nothing else on the shelf.
description:
Silver-marbled hearts on thread-fine stems that will hang a metre from a high shelf. It is a succulent underneath it all, so let it dry out between waterings.

  • Light: Bright, indirect
  • Water: Every two weeks, let it dry between
  • Pets: Safe
  • Trails to: 1 m
  • Difficulty: Easy

name: Terracotta Pot
short_description: Unglazed terracotta with a drainage hole and a matching saucer.
description: Unglazed clay breathes, which is why terracotta forgives a heavy hand with the watering can. Comes with a saucer, in the same three sizes as the plants.

name: Stoneware Pot
short_description: Speckled stoneware with a matte glaze, glazed inside.
description: Thrown stoneware with a soft matte glaze and a sealed interior, so it holds water rather than marking a shelf. Reduced while we clear the sand colourway.

name: Hanging Planter
short_description: A glazed pot in a cotton rope cradle, for trailing plants.
description: A shallow glazed pot held in a hand-knotted cotton cradle, hung from a brass ring. Made for a pothos or a string of hearts on a high shelf.

name: Watering Can
short_description: Brass, one litre, with a long spout that reaches the back row.
description: A long thin spout gets under the leaves and into the soil, where the water belongs. One litre, which is three or four plants before a refill.

reviews.author: Tom H.
reviews.content: The spout is the whole point. I stopped soaking the leaves and the calathea stopped sulking.

name: Potting Mix, 10 L
short_description: Peat-free compost with bark and perlite, for houseplants.
description: Peat-free, with bark for structure and perlite for drainage, mixed for pots rather than borders. Ten litres repots about four medium plants.

name: Plant Food, 250 ml
short_description: A balanced feed for the growing months, diluted in the can.
description: Five millilitres in a litre of water, every other watering from March to September, and nothing at all through the winter.
